# 7 Anomalies

Anomalies are observations that deviate significantly from expected behavior.

In time series this means:

- strong deviation from the trend
- strong deviation from the seasonal pattern
- sudden structural breaks

Important: anomalies are **context-dependent**.

---

::: {.callout-note title="Remember"}
An anomaly is not purely a statistical property.  
It is a deviation from the expected behavior of a process.
:::

---

## 7.1 Example Signal with Outliers

::: {#f85cdd4d .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

rng = np.random.default_rng(99)

t = pd.date_range("2025-01-01", periods=24*10, freq="h")
trend = np.linspace(0, 2, len(t))
season = 0.8 * np.sin(2*np.pi*(t.hour)/24)
noise = 0.3 * rng.normal(size=len(t))

s = pd.Series(10 + trend + season + noise, index=t, name="signal")

# artificial anomalies
s.iloc[40] += 4
s.iloc[120] -= 3

s.plot(title="Signal with Anomalies")
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![](07-anomalien_files/figure-html/cell-2-output-1.png){width=566 height=461}
:::
:::

## 7.2 Global Z-Score Method

We standardize the entire time series.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Pandas

::: {#6e4ecf83 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
z = (s - s.mean()) / s.std()
anomalies = s[abs(z) > 3]

ax = s.plot(label="Signal")
anomalies.plot(ax=ax, linestyle="None", marker="o", label="Anomaly")
plt.legend()
plt.title("Anomalies (Z-Score)")
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![](07-anomalien_files/figure-html/cell-3-output-1.png){width=566 height=461}
:::
:::


## NumPy

::: {#4cf22079 .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
y = s.to_numpy()

z_np = (y - np.mean(y)) / np.std(y)
anomalies_idx = np.where(np.abs(z_np) > 3)[0]

plt.plot(y, label="Signal")
plt.scatter(anomalies_idx, y[anomalies_idx], label="Anomaly")
plt.legend()
plt.title("Anomalies (NumPy Z-Score)")
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![](07-anomalien_files/figure-html/cell-4-output-1.png){width=577 height=431}
:::
:::


:::

---

::: {.callout-warning title="Warning"}
Z-score performs poorly when there is a strong trend or seasonality,
because global means can become distorted.
:::

---

## 7.3 Local Anomaly (Baseline + Residual)

Instead of global standardization, we define a local baseline.

::: {#728e1769 .cell execution_count=4}
``` {.python .cell-code}
baseline = s.ewm(span=24, adjust=False).mean()
residual = s - baseline

score = (residual - residual.mean()) / residual.std()
anomalies_local = s[abs(score) > 3]

ax = s.plot(alpha=0.6, label="Signal")
baseline.plot(ax=ax, label="Baseline")
anomalies_local.plot(ax=ax, linestyle="None", marker="o", label="Anomaly")
plt.legend()
plt.title("Local Anomalies (EWMA Baseline)")
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![](07-anomalien_files/figure-html/cell-5-output-1.png){width=566 height=461}
:::
:::


---

::: {.callout-tip title="Interpretation"}
Local methods are more robust
when a trend or seasonality is present.
:::

---

## 7.4 Rolling Standard Deviation

Anomalies can also be defined as strong deviations
relative to the local variance.

::: {#8ba85518 .cell execution_count=5}
``` {.python .cell-code}
rolling_std = s.rolling("24h").std()
rolling_mean = s.rolling("24h").mean()

upper = rolling_mean + 3 * rolling_std
lower = rolling_mean - 3 * rolling_std

ax = s.plot(label="Signal")
upper.plot(ax=ax, linestyle="--", label="Upper Bound")
lower.plot(ax=ax, linestyle="--", label="Lower Bound")
plt.legend()
plt.title("Anomalies via Rolling Bounds")
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![](07-anomalien_files/figure-html/cell-6-output-1.png){width=566 height=461}
:::
:::


---

## 7.5 Structural Break vs Outlier

A single peak → Outlier  
A permanent level shift → Structural Break

Both require different interpretation.

---

::: {.callout-note title="Methodological Note"}
Before marking anomalies:

1. Check the trend  
2. Check seasonality  
3. Define the baseline  
4. Justify the threshold  
:::

---

## 7.6 Mini-Exercises

1. Remove the trend before applying the Z-score.  
   - How does the result change?

2. Lower the threshold from 3 to 2.  
   - What happens?

3. Simulate a permanent level jump.  
   - Is it detected as an anomaly?
